laws.title: 0.03% BAC Driving Limit
laws.subtitle: Japan's strict drink-driving threshold applies in Aichi
laws.fullDescription: Under the Road Traffic Act (道路交通法), driving with a BAC of 0.03% or above is a criminal offence. Aichi Prefecture Police enforce this rigorously — Aichi has historically had one of Japan's highest rates of traffic fatalities and has run sustained anti-drunk driving campaigns since the early 2000s.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment or ¥500,000 fine; licence suspension
exceptions: Commercial drivers are held to zero-tolerance standard

quiz.q: What BAC limit does Japan enforce for driving in Aichi?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Road Traffic Act sets the BAC limit at 0.03%, among the strictest in the world.

laws.title: Toyota Production System Safety Standards
laws.subtitle: Aichi's automotive factories operate under strict labour safety rules
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture is Japan's automotive manufacturing heartland, home to Toyota, Denso, and hundreds of suppliers. The Aichi Labour Bureau enforces the Industrial Safety and Health Act (労働安全衛生法) with particular rigour in automated assembly lines, requiring robot safety barriers, daily machine inspections, and designated safety supervisors on every shift.
laws.penalty: Up to ¥3,000,000 fine; production suspension; criminal prosecution for managerial negligence causing death
exceptions: R&D prototype workshops may use modified safety layouts with approved risk assessments

quiz.q: Which global automotive company is headquartered in Aichi Prefecture?
quiz.explanation: Toyota is headquartered in Toyota City, Aichi Prefecture, making it Japan's automotive manufacturing heartland.

laws.title: Aichi Industrial Emissions Control Ordinance
laws.subtitle: Dense manufacturing base faces strict air quality monitoring
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture's Pollution Prevention Ordinance (公害防止条例) requires all factories emitting NOx, SOx, or particulate matter above threshold levels to install continuous monitoring and submit quarterly reports to the prefecture. Following 1970s Yokkaichi disease cases nearby (Mie Prefecture), Aichi adopted some of Japan's toughest standards for industrial air quality.
laws.penalty: Up to ¥3,000,000 fine or 1 year imprisonment; factory closure for serious violations
exceptions: Small workshops under specified emission thresholds use simplified annual self-reporting

quiz.q: What nearby 1970s disease prompted Aichi to adopt strict industrial air quality standards?
quiz.explanation: The Yokkaichi asthma cases in nearby Mie Prefecture prompted stringent industrial emissions controls throughout the region.

laws.title: Nagoya Castle Reconstruction Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Japan's most ambitious castle restoration project has strict rules
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya Castle (名古屋城), home of Japan's most ambitious wooden donjon reconstruction project, is a designated Special Historic Site (特別史跡). All construction and archaeological work requires Agency for Cultural Affairs approval. The ongoing wooden reconstruction (target completion 2030s) uses traditional techniques under strict supervision. The original concrete-reinforced structure was closed for safety assessment in 2018.
laws.penalty: Up to 5 years imprisonment for damage to a Special Historic Site; fines for unauthorised excavation
exceptions: Approved conservation-grade contractors working under cultural agency permits are exempt

quiz.q: What makes Nagoya Castle's current restoration project historically significant?
options: It uses concrete for earthquake safety
It is Japan's most ambitious traditional wooden donjon reconstruction
It is being relocated to a new site
It is the oldest castle in Japan
quiz.explanation: Nagoya Castle is undergoing Japan's most ambitious wooden donjon reconstruction using traditional techniques.

laws.title: Nagoya City Noise Regulation Ordinance
laws.subtitle: Night noise limits strictly enforced in Japan's fourth-largest city
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya City's Pollution Prevention Ordinance sets noise limits of 60 dB(A) during day hours in residential areas, dropping to 45 dB(A) at night (22:00–06:00). Construction near schools or hospitals requires advance notice and must cease by 20:00. Nagoya's dense grid of residential and commercial zones makes noise regulation especially complex.
laws.penalty: Fines up to ¥500,000; stop-work orders for persistent violations
exceptions: Emergency public works with city approval may operate outside standard hours

quiz.q: What is the nighttime noise limit in Nagoya residential areas?
quiz.explanation: Nagoya's ordinance limits nighttime noise in residential zones to 45 dB(A).

laws.title: Aichi Flood Control Building Regulations
laws.subtitle: Homes in Aichi's low-lying Nobi Plain face flood-proofing requirements
laws.fullDescription: Aichi's Nobi Plain — among the lowest-lying inhabited areas in Japan — is protected by an elaborate tidal embankment (スーパー堤防) system. Under the River Act (河川法) and Aichi's Disaster Prevention Plan, new residential construction in designated flood hazard zones requires raised foundations (minimum 1 metre above road level), flood doors, and connection to the city's flood alert notification system.
laws.penalty: Building permit refusal for non-compliant designs; fines for constructing without flood zone approval
exceptions: Industrial buildings with separate flood impact assessments may use equivalent alternative measures

quiz.q: What is the minimum raised foundation height required in Aichi's flood hazard zones?
quiz.explanation: New residential construction in Aichi's flood hazard zones must have foundations raised at least 1 metre above road level.

laws.title: Nagoya Cuisine Trademark Protections
laws.subtitle: Miso katsu, hitsumabushi, and kishimen are protected regional foods
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya's distinctive cuisine (名古屋めし, Nagoya-meshi) includes internationally known dishes like miso katsu (味噌カツ) and hitsumabushi (ひつまぶし, eel over rice). Under the Act on Protection of Intellectual Property and regional certification guidelines, certain Nagoya food brands are trademarked by industry associations. Restaurants advertising these as 'genuine Nagoya-meshi' must meet ingredient and preparation standards set by the relevant guild.
laws.penalty: Civil trademark claims; loss of regional certification for misleading advertising
exceptions: Home cooking and non-commercial social media references are not regulated

quiz.q: What is the Japanese term for Nagoya's distinctive local cuisine?
quiz.explanation: Nagoya's distinctive local cuisine is called Nagoya-meshi (名古屋めし), including miso katsu and hitsumabushi.

laws.title: Aichi Multicultural Support for Brazilian Community
laws.subtitle: Aichi has Japan's largest Brazilian community with dedicated support rules
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture has Japan's largest Brazilian Nikkei community, concentrated in Toyota City and Hamamatsu-adjacent areas. Aichi's Multicultural Coexistence Policy (多文化共生推進プラン) mandates Portuguese-language public services at city halls, schools, and hospitals. Employers of foreign workers must provide Japanese language training subsidised by the prefecture.
laws.penalty: No specific penalty; violations of anti-discrimination employment rules reported to Aichi Labour Bureau
exceptions: Small businesses under 10 employees are exempt from mandatory language training obligations

quiz.q: What language is specifically mandated in Aichi public services for its large immigrant community?
quiz.explanation: Aichi mandates Portuguese-language public services due to its large Brazilian Nikkei community.

laws.title: Chubu Centrair Airport Restricted Zone Rules
laws.subtitle: Japan's 5th-busiest airport has strict access and noise regulations
laws.fullDescription: Chubu Centrair International Airport (中部国際空港), built on a man-made island in Ise Bay, operates under the Civil Aeronautics Act and national airport noise regulations. Night flights are prohibited between 23:00 and 06:00. The surrounding Ise Bay fishery exclusion zone prohibits fishing vessels within 500 metres of approach and departure corridors. Security perimeters are enforced under the Aviation Hijacking Prevention Act.
laws.penalty: Fines for violating flight curfew; criminal prosecution for security zone breaches
exceptions: Emergency and cargo freighter flights may operate with authority approval during curfew hours

quiz.q: On which type of structure is Chubu Centrair International Airport built?
quiz.explanation: Chubu Centrair International Airport was built on a man-made island in Ise Bay, opening in 2005.

laws.title: Aichi Monozukuri SME Support Programme
laws.subtitle: Prefecture subsidises manufacturing SMEs through special finance schemes
laws.fullDescription: Aichi's Monozukuri (ものづくり) SME Support Programme provides subsidised low-interest loans and equipment investment grants to small and medium manufacturers through Aichi Bank and prefecture-guaranteed credit. Firms receiving support must maintain a minimum of 5 full-time employees, file annual financial reports, and not commence bankruptcy proceedings within 3 years of receiving support.
laws.penalty: Full clawback of grants plus interest if eligibility conditions are breached within 3 years
exceptions: Force majeure business interruptions (natural disaster, pandemic) reviewed case-by-case for clawback waiver

quiz.q: What does the Japanese term 'monozukuri' (ものづくり) mean?
options: The art of making things / craftsmanship
quiz.explanation: Monozukuri (ものづくり) means 'the art of making things' and embodies Japan's manufacturing craftsmanship philosophy.

laws.title: Aichi Flower and Greenhouse Industry Regulations
laws.subtitle: Japan's top flower-producing prefecture has strict quality standards
laws.fullDescription: Aichi is Japan's largest flower-producing prefecture, particularly chrysanthemums (菊), carnations, and orchids used in ceremonies nationwide. Under the JAS Act and Aichi Flower Promotion Ordinance, commercial flower producers must use certified pesticide applications and maintain hygiene records for export flowers. Aichi produces flowers for the imperial household's ceremonial events under special quality protocols.
laws.penalty: Licence suspension for pesticide misuse; fines under the JAS Act for grade mislabelling
exceptions: Small hobby growers selling at farmers' markets under ¥300,000 annual revenue use simplified registration

quiz.q: Which flower is Aichi Prefecture's most famous agricultural product?
quiz.explanation: Aichi is Japan's largest chrysanthemum producer, supplying flowers for nationwide ceremonies and the imperial household.

laws.title: Tokai Earthquake Preparedness Orders
laws.subtitle: Aichi is in Japan's highest-risk earthquake anticipation zone
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture sits in the Tokai Earthquake Anticipation Zone (東海地震対策地域). Under the Large-Scale Earthquake Special Measures Act (大規模地震対策特別措置法), the government may issue an Earthquake Warning (警戒宣言) before a predicted Tokai earthquake. Upon such a warning, Aichi Prefecture and all municipalities must immediately implement pre-planned emergency responses: closing schools, activating evacuation centres, and deploying pre-positioned supplies.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalty for residents, but failure of businesses designated as essential emergency functions to activate plans triggers administrative sanctions
exceptions: International visitors receive early warning through the J-Alert system broadcast in multiple languages

quiz.q: What special law governs Aichi's preparedness for the anticipated Tokai earthquake?
quiz.explanation: The Large-Scale Earthquake Special Measures Act governs the Tokai Earthquake anticipation zone, which includes Aichi Prefecture.

laws.title: Ise Grand Shrine Approach Road Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Access roads to Japan's holiest shrine complex have special rules
laws.fullDescription: While Ise Grand Shrine (伊勢神宮) itself is in Mie Prefecture, its approach roads (おはらい町, Oharaimachi) pass through Aichi-administered zones. Aichi Prefecture's transport management and the Aichi-Mie cross-prefectural coordinating body manage tourist traffic, particularly during the Ise Shima National Park tourism peak. Large vehicles are banned on approach roads during shrine festivals under the Road Traffic Act special provisions.
laws.penalty: Fines ¥10,000–¥50,000 for large vehicles in restricted approach zones during designated festival periods
exceptions: Authorised delivery vehicles for shrine facilities may use rear service roads

quiz.q: What is the shopping street near Ise Grand Shrine called?
quiz.explanation: Oharaimachi (おはらい町) is the traditional shopping street approaching Ise Grand Shrine, subject to vehicle restrictions during festivals.

laws.title: Aichi Anti-Organised Crime Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Prefecture targets organised crime with enhanced exclusion rules
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture's Organised Crime Group Exclusion Ordinance (暴力団排除条例) requires all businesses in Aichi to include anti-gang clauses in contracts. Following incidents involving the Kodo-kai (弘道会), a Yamaguchi-gumi affiliated group particularly active in Aichi, the prefecture reinforced enforcement in construction, real estate, and waste disposal industries.
laws.penalty: Business name publication; up to 1 year imprisonment for serious cases; fines for businesses failing to report extortion
exceptions: Businesses that immediately report extortion and cooperate with police receive protection from co-liability

quiz.q: Which organised crime group is particularly associated with Aichi Prefecture?
quiz.explanation: The Kodo-kai (弘道会), a Yamaguchi-gumi affiliate, is particularly active in Aichi Prefecture.

laws.title: Aichi Indoor Smoking Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Prefectural and national indoor smoking rules fully apply
laws.fullDescription: Under the Health Promotion Act (健康増進法) as amended in 2020 and Aichi Prefecture's supplementary ordinance, smoking is prohibited inside all restaurants, bars, hotels, and entertainment venues. The prefecture was among the later adopters of pre-national ordinances but now fully implements the stricter 2020 national rules. All enclosed workplaces are smoke-free; outdoor designated smoking rooms must be ventilated and sealed.
laws.penalty: Fines up to ¥50,000 for facility operators who fail to enforce the smoking ban
exceptions: Designated ventilated smoking rooms with appropriate signage are permitted in commercial buildings

quiz.q: In which year did Japan's national indoor smoking ban fully take effect in Aichi?
quiz.explanation: Japan's Health Promotion Act amendment, fully banning indoor smoking in public places, took effect in 2020.

laws.title: Nagoya Protocol on Biodiversity — Local Implementation
laws.subtitle: Aichi hosts the secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture is historically significant for international biodiversity law: the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing (2010) and the Aichi Targets (CBD COP10) were agreed in Nagoya. In recognition, Aichi Prefecture enforces strict biodiversity-sensitive land development rules. Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) for large developments must include biodiversity surveys, and developers must prepare mitigation plans for any impact on designated habitats.
laws.penalty: EIA non-compliance triggers project suspension; fines up to ¥3,000,000 for illegal development in protected habitats
exceptions: Small-scale agricultural land improvements under 0.5 hectares are exempt from full EIA requirements

quiz.q: What major international biodiversity agreement was signed in Nagoya, Aichi, in 2010?
options: Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing
quiz.explanation: The Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing (CBD) was agreed in Nagoya, Aichi, in 2010.

laws.title: Aichi Technical High School Industry Partnership Rules
laws.subtitle: Aichi's vocation schools have special arrangements with automotive manufacturers
laws.fullDescription: Aichi's prefectural technical high schools (工業高校) have industry partnership programmes with Toyota, Denso, and other manufacturers. Under the School Education Act and Aichi Prefecture Education Board guidelines, students undertaking practical industry placements must be covered by workplace accident insurance and must not be engaged in hazardous operations. Industry partners must appoint a certified supervisor for all high school interns.
laws.penalty: Loss of placement approval for companies that violate intern safety rules; school disciplinary review for non-compliant teachers
exceptions: University-level interns and adult technical training programmes operate under different frameworks

quiz.q: What must industry partners provide when hosting Aichi technical high school students?
options: A certified supervisor for all high school interns
quiz.explanation: Industry partners hosting Aichi technical high school interns must appoint a certified supervisor for all students.

laws.title: Nagoya Municipal Subway Lost Property Rules
laws.subtitle: Lost items on Nagoya Subway are handled under railway regulations
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya Municipal Subway (名古屋市営地下鉄) operates under the Railway Business Act (鉄道事業法) and the Lost Property Act (遺失物法). Found items must be turned in to the nearest station within 24 hours of discovery. Valuable items not claimed within 3 months go to Nagoya City. Cash found on the system that is not claimed is transferred to the finder after 3 months, minus a 10% handling fee to the city.
laws.penalty: Up to ¥30,000 fine or 1 year imprisonment for appropriating found property without reporting it
exceptions: Perishable items or mobile phones with identifying information may be returned to owners using contact details displayed

quiz.q: How long must Nagoya Subway found cash remain unclaimed before the finder may receive it?
quiz.explanation: Unclaimed found cash on Nagoya Subway is transferred to the finder after 3 months, minus a 10% handling fee.

laws.title: Noh and Kyogen Theatre Heritage Protections in Aichi
laws.subtitle: Classical performing arts venues have special maintenance grants
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture hosts active Noh (能) and Kyogen (狂言) performance traditions. Designated Noh stages (能舞台) classified as Important Cultural Properties must be maintained using traditional carpentry techniques approved by the Agency for Cultural Affairs. Aichi's prefectural grant programme subsidises maintenance of privately-owned Noh stages open to the public at least 3 times per year.
laws.penalty: Loss of subsidy; fines for unauthorised structural alterations to designated stages
exceptions: Stages used exclusively for private family ceremonies may receive heritage designation without public access requirements

quiz.q: How many times per year must a privately-owned Noh stage in Aichi open to the public to qualify for prefecture maintenance grants?
quiz.explanation: Aichi's grant programme requires privately-owned Noh stages to be open to the public at least 3 times per year.

laws.title: Aichi Used Vehicle Dealer Licensing
laws.subtitle: Japan's automotive hub has stringent used car trade regulations
laws.fullDescription: Aichi, the heart of Japan's automotive industry, has the highest concentration of used vehicle dealers in Japan. Under the Used Goods Dealer Licencing Act (古物商許可法) as enforced by Aichi Prefectural Police, all dealers must be licensed, maintain records of all vehicle purchases (including VIN and seller identity), and report suspicious vehicles to the police within 5 days. Odometer tampering carries severe criminal penalties.
laws.penalty: Up to 10 years imprisonment and ¥5,000,000 fine for odometer tampering; licence revocation for record-keeping failures
exceptions: Auto parts-only dealers not reselling whole vehicles use a simplified parts trader licence
laws.sourceLabel: Aichi Prefectural Police Used Goods Division

quiz.q: Within how many days must Aichi used car dealers report suspicious vehicles to police?
quiz.explanation: Aichi used vehicle dealers must report suspicious vehicles to police within 5 days of acquisition.

laws.title: Aichi Foreign Resident Support Centres
laws.subtitle: Prefecture operates multilingual one-stop centres for foreign residents
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture operates the Aichi Multicultural Center (愛知県多文化共生推進室) and a network of foreign resident support offices in Toyota City, Nagoya, and Toyohashi. Foreign nationals must register their address within 14 days under the Immigration Control Act. The centres provide Portuguese, Spanish, Chinese, Vietnamese, and English assistance for registration, healthcare, and children's school enrolment.
laws.penalty: Up to ¥200,000 fine for failure to register address; deportation in serious cases
exceptions: Short-stay tourists with visa exemptions are not required to register

quiz.q: Within how many days must foreign nationals register their address in Aichi?
quiz.explanation: Foreign nationals residing in Aichi must register their address within 14 days under the Immigration Control Act.

laws.title: Nagoya Grampus and Chunichi Dragon Stadium Safety Rules
laws.subtitle: Aichi sports venues must comply with event safety ordinances
laws.fullDescription: Toyota Stadium (Nagoya Grampus football) and Vantelin Dome Nagoya (Chunichi Dragons baseball) operate under Aichi Prefecture's Large Venue Safety Ordinance and the national Sports Safety Act. Events expecting over 10,000 spectators require pre-event safety plans submitted to Aichi Police. Alcohol sales must cease 30 minutes before the end of matches. Re-entry after leaving the venue is prohibited except with a special re-entry stamp.
laws.penalty: Event cancellation for non-submitted safety plans; fines for alcohol sales violations
exceptions: Private corporate hospitality suites may continue serving alcohol under different rules

quiz.q: When must alcohol sales cease at Aichi Prefecture sports venues?
options: 30 minutes before the end of matches
At the start of the 2nd half
quiz.explanation: Alcohol sales at Aichi Prefecture sports venues must cease 30 minutes before the end of matches.

laws.title: Aichi Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Rules
laws.subtitle: EEE waste must be sorted and disposed of via certified recyclers
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture, with its massive electronics manufacturing sector (Denso, Aisin, etc.), generates significant volumes of waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE). Under the Home Appliance Recycling Act (家電リサイクル法) and Small Home Appliance Recycling Act (小型家電リサイクル法), consumers must return specified appliances to retailers or approved collection points. Industrial WEEE from factories must be handled by certified industrial waste contractors.
laws.penalty: Fines up to ¥3,000,000 for industrial WEEE illegal disposal; consumers face collection fee surcharges for non-compliant disposal
exceptions: Ultra-small electronic components under 10 grams total weight can be disposed of with burnable waste

quiz.q: Under which law must consumers return major household appliances for recycling in Aichi?
options: Home Appliance Recycling Act (家電リサイクル法)
quiz.explanation: The Home Appliance Recycling Act (家電リサイクル法) requires consumers to return specified appliances to retailers or approved recycling points.

laws.title: Nagoya Urban Regeneration Special Zone Rules
laws.subtitle: Central Nagoya has deregulated development zones to attract investment
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya's Sakae and Meieki (Nagoya Station) districts are designated Urban Regeneration Special Zones under the Urban Regeneration Special Measures Act (都市再生特別措置法). Developers in these zones may exceed standard floor-area ratios by up to 50% if they contribute public open space or underground pedestrian connections. The Aichi Sky Expo and Meieki redevelopment operate under these special zone permissions.
laws.penalty: Permit withdrawal for developments that do not deliver the agreed public space contributions
exceptions: Historic buildings within special zones are exempt from floor-area ratio bonuses but may be retained

quiz.q: By how much may developers in Nagoya's Urban Regeneration Special Zones exceed standard floor-area ratios?
quiz.explanation: Developers in Nagoya's Urban Regeneration Special Zones may exceed standard floor-area ratios by up to 50% if they contribute public open space.

laws.title: Nagoya City Partnership Recognition Scheme
laws.subtitle: Nagoya recognises same-sex partnerships for city services
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya City launched its Partnership and Cohabitation Relationship Certification Scheme (パートナーシップ・ファミリーシップ制度) in 2022, recognising same-sex couples and their children for city housing applications, emergency room next-of-kin status, and city hospital visitation rights. The scheme was expanded in 2023 to include cohabiting adults caring for elderly relatives.
laws.penalty: False declarations may result in certificate revocation
exceptions: National family registry (戸籍) rights are unchanged; this applies only to city-level services

quiz.q: In which year did Nagoya City launch its Partnership and Cohabitation Relationship Certification?
quiz.explanation: Nagoya City launched its Partnership and Cohabitation Relationship Certification Scheme in 2022.

laws.title: Aichi Typhoon Evacuation Protocols
laws.subtitle: Aichi regularly faces severe typhoons requiring prefecture-wide evacuation orders
laws.fullDescription: Aichi's location on the Pacific coast makes it one of Japan's most typhoon-vulnerable prefectures. Under the Disaster Countermeasures Basic Act (災害対策基本法), Aichi's 5-level evacuation order system requires municipalities to issue Level 3 (High-Risk Individuals Evacuate) orders when typhoons are forecast above a defined threshold. The 1959 Isewan Typhoon, which killed over 5,000 in Aichi, led to permanent embankment upgrades and emergency response protocols.
laws.penalty: Non-compliance with evacuation orders carries no criminal penalty but may affect insurance and disaster relief eligibility
exceptions: Persons who cannot physically evacuate receive coordinated emergency assistance from the prefecture

quiz.q: How many people were killed in Aichi by the 1959 Isewan Typhoon, leading to permanent flood defences?
quiz.explanation: The 1959 Isewan Typhoon killed over 5,000 people in Aichi, leading to permanent embankment upgrades and emergency response protocols.

laws.title: Aichi Export Control for Dual-Use Technologies
laws.subtitle: Automotive and aerospace manufacturers must comply with export controls
laws.fullDescription: Aichi's automotive, aerospace (Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Komaki), and industrial robot manufacturers export dual-use technologies worldwide. Under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act (外国為替及び外国貿易法), manufacturers must obtain export licences for items on Japan's Foreign Exchange Control List. Aichi prefecture coordinates with METI's Nagoya Regional Export Control Office for compliance guidance.
laws.penalty: Up to 10 years imprisonment and ¥30,000,000 fine for exporting controlled items without licence
exceptions: Purely civilian components below specified thresholds are exempt from export licence requirements

quiz.q: Under which Japanese law are dual-use technology exports from Aichi controlled?
options: Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act (外為法)
quiz.explanation: Japan's Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act (外為法) controls dual-use technology exports, enforced by METI in Aichi.

laws.title: Aichi Rice Brand Certification — Aichi no Kaori
laws.subtitle: Aichi's premium rice brand is protected by prefecture co-operative
laws.fullDescription: Aichi no Kaori (愛知のかおり), Aichi Prefecture's premium rice variety, is registered under the Plant Variety Protection Act (種苗法) and marketed by JA Aichi. Only certified producers growing the specific variety in approved Aichi growing areas may use the name. Seed reproduction for commercial sale requires a licence from the original breeder. The variety was developed by Aichi Prefectural Agricultural Research Center.
laws.penalty: Up to ¥3,000,000 fine under the Plant Variety Protection Act for unauthorised seed reproduction or brand misuse
exceptions: Farmers may save seeds for their own planting under the registered variety's specific terms

quiz.q: What is Aichi Prefecture's certified premium rice brand?
options: Aichi no Kaori (愛知のかおり)
quiz.explanation: Aichi no Kaori (愛知のかおり) is Aichi Prefecture's protected premium rice variety, developed by the Aichi Agricultural Research Center.

laws.title: Industrial Robot Safety Regulations — Aichi
laws.subtitle: Robot operators in Aichi's factories require certified training
laws.fullDescription: Aichi leads Japan in industrial robot density, with Toyota's assembly lines operating thousands of robotic units. Under the Industrial Safety and Health Act Regulations (労働安全衛生規則), workers who operate, adjust, or maintain industrial robots weighing over 80kg must hold a robot operation special training certificate (産業用ロボット特別教育). Safety barriers (柵) must surround all operational robot cells; entering during operation is prohibited.
laws.penalty: Up to ¥500,000 fine for employers allowing uncertified workers to operate industrial robots; criminal negligence prosecution for resulting injuries
exceptions: Collaborative robots (cobots) under specific safety standards may operate without physical barriers with approved risk assessments

quiz.q: What weight threshold triggers the requirement for special training certification to operate industrial robots in Aichi?
quiz.explanation: Workers operating industrial robots weighing over 80kg in Aichi must hold a special training certificate under safety regulations.

laws.title: Aichi Infectious Disease Quarantine — Chubu Airport
laws.subtitle: Chubu Centrair operates active quarantine inspection under infectious disease law
laws.fullDescription: Chubu Centrair International Airport's Quarantine Station, operated by the Ministry of Health, screens arriving passengers under the Infectious Disease Control Law (感染症法). During epidemics designated by the Minister of Health, airport staff may require temperature checks, health questionnaire submissions, and medical examination. Passengers who refuse examination may be placed in quarantine accommodation.
laws.penalty: Up to ¥300,000 fine for refusing quarantine examination during a designated infectious disease period
exceptions: Diplomatic passengers and flight crew may use expedited health screening processes
laws.sourceLabel: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare — Chubu Quarantine Station

quiz.q: What may happen to passengers at Chubu Airport who refuse health examination during an epidemic?
options: Fine only, no restriction on movement
quiz.explanation: Passengers refusing examination during a designated epidemic period at Chubu Airport may be placed in quarantine accommodation.

laws.title: Inuyama Castle — Oldest Surviving Original Castle Keep
laws.subtitle: Japan's oldest original wooden castle keep has strict preservation rules
laws.fullDescription: Inuyama Castle (犬山城) in Aichi is one of Japan's twelve original surviving castle keeps and a National Treasure (国宝). Under the Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties (文化財保護法), no modification, construction, or excavation within 100 metres of the castle perimeter is permitted without Agency for Cultural Affairs approval. Until 2004, Inuyama Castle was the only castle in Japan owned by a private individual (the Naruse family).
laws.penalty: Up to ¥5,000,000 fine or 5 years imprisonment for damaging a National Treasure; construction permit refusal in protection zone
exceptions: Approved restoration works by certified craftsmen under cultural agency supervision are permitted

quiz.q: What makes Inuyama Castle unique among Japan's twelve original castle keeps?
options: It is made of stone not wood
quiz.explanation: Until 2004, Inuyama Castle was the only castle in Japan owned by a private individual — the Naruse family.

laws.title: Nagoya Station Redevelopment Safety Rules
laws.subtitle: Japan's largest floor area station complex has strict safety and access rules
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya Station (名古屋駅), containing the JR Central Towers and Midland Square, is one of the world's largest station complexes by floor area. Under the Building Standards Act and Nagoya City's Safety Ordinance, all pedestrian flows through the underground concourse must be monitored and crowd density must not exceed 2 persons per square metre at choke points. Emergency evacuation routes must be clearly marked and must not be obstructed by commercial stalls.
laws.penalty: Fines up to ¥1,000,000 for businesses obstructing emergency evacuation routes; city may order immediate removal
exceptions: Temporary licensed market stalls have designated zones that do not block emergency routes

quiz.q: What crowd density limit applies to Nagoya Station underground concourse choke points?
quiz.explanation: Nagoya Station's safety rules limit crowd density at choke points to no more than 2 persons per square metre.

laws.title: Ise Bay Fishery Protection Zone
laws.subtitle: Aichi's coastline on Ise Bay has strict fishery conservation rules
laws.fullDescription: Ise Bay (伊勢湾), shared by Aichi and Mie Prefectures, was designated a Special Case Sea Area under the Water Pollution Control Act following severe eutrophication in the 1970s. Industrial wastewater discharge into Ise Bay tributaries must meet COD limits of 10mg/L. Aquaculture licences for Aichi-side operations are issued by the Aichi Fisheries Cooperative and capped annually to prevent overfishing of tiger prawns (kuruma-ebi) and clams (hamaguri).
laws.penalty: Up to ¥3,000,000 fine for discharging non-compliant wastewater; licence revocation for aquaculture violations
exceptions: Non-commercial personal recreational fishing from shore is not subject to aquaculture licence requirements

quiz.q: What water quality parameter is specifically regulated for Ise Bay wastewater discharge?
quiz.explanation: Industrial wastewater discharging into Ise Bay must meet a COD limit of 10mg/L under Aichi's special case sea area rules.

laws.title: Aichi Child Welfare and Anti-Abuse Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Prefecture tripled child welfare officers following high-profile cases
laws.fullDescription: Following several nationally reported child abuse cases in Aichi, the prefecture significantly expanded its Children's Welfare Center (児童相談所) capacity and powers. Under the Child Abuse Prevention Act (児童虐待防止法), welfare officers may enter homes without parental consent when abuse is strongly suspected, and police must cooperate. Mandatory reporters — teachers, doctors, nursery workers — who fail to report suspected abuse face administrative sanctions.
laws.penalty: Administrative sanctions for mandatory reporters who fail to report; criminal prosecution for obstruction of welfare officers
exceptions: Corporal punishment by parents has been explicitly prohibited since the 2020 Civil Code amendment

quiz.q: Who are mandatory reporters of suspected child abuse in Aichi under Japanese law?
quiz.explanation: Teachers, doctors, nursery workers, and other professionals in contact with children are mandatory reporters under Japan's Child Abuse Prevention Act.

laws.title: Nagoya Stock Exchange Listing Rules
laws.subtitle: NSE-listed companies must comply with Nagoya-specific disclosure standards
laws.fullDescription: The Nagoya Stock Exchange (名古屋証券取引所), one of Japan's three remaining regional exchanges, lists many Aichi-based manufacturers. Listed companies must comply with NSE's disclosure rules and the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act (金融商品取引法). NSE's Premier Market requires minimum equity of ¥2 billion and annual disclosure of sustainability (ESG) reports. NSE merged trading systems with Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2014 but retains independent listing standards.
laws.penalty: Delisting; fines up to ¥5,000,000 under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act for false disclosures
exceptions: The NSE Centrex market for startups has lower listing thresholds and simplified disclosure requirements

quiz.q: What is the minimum equity requirement for Nagoya Stock Exchange's Premier Market listing?
quiz.explanation: NSE's Premier Market requires a minimum equity of ¥2 billion for listed companies.

laws.title: LEGOLAND Japan Theme Park Safety Rules
laws.subtitle: Nagoya's LEGOLAND operates under strict amusement park safety regulations
laws.fullDescription: LEGOLAND Japan, located in Nagoya's Minato Ward, operates under the Amusement Attractions Safety Act (遊戯施設の安全基準) and MLIT guidelines. All ride operators must be at least 18, hold a ride safety certification, and conduct pre-opening daily equipment inspections. Height restrictions on rides must be enforced, and the park must submit annual safety reports to Aichi Prefecture.
laws.penalty: Park suspension for operating rides with failed safety inspections; fines up to ¥3,000,000 for safety record falsification
exceptions: Soft-play indoor areas and non-mechanical attractions are subject to lighter inspection requirements
laws.sourceLabel: LEGOLAND Japan / Aichi Prefecture Tourism Division

quiz.q: What must LEGOLAND Japan ride operators do before the park opens each day?
quiz.explanation: Ride operators at LEGOLAND Japan must conduct pre-opening daily equipment inspections under Aichi's amusement park safety rules.

laws.title: Nagoya Night-Time Business Licensing
laws.subtitle: Sakae entertainment district businesses must hold amusement licences
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya's Sakae district, the city's primary entertainment hub, has a concentration of hostess bars, karaoke, and late-night food businesses. Under the Act on Control and Improvement of Amusement Business (風営法), businesses must hold category-specific licences. Minors may not enter Category 1 establishments after 18:00. Aichi Police conduct periodic compliance checks and may revoke licences for violations.
laws.penalty: Licence suspension for admitting minors; fines up to ¥2,000,000 for operating without a valid category licence
exceptions: Restaurants open until midnight without entertainment elements are exempt from wind-ei licensing
laws.sourceLabel: Aichi Prefectural Police Wind Business Division

quiz.q: What is the name of Nagoya's primary entertainment and nightlife district?
quiz.explanation: Sakae is Nagoya's primary entertainment hub, with a high concentration of licensed amusement businesses.

laws.title: Aichi Medical Cluster — Nagoya University Hospital Rules
laws.subtitle: Large tertiary hospitals in Aichi operate under strict accreditation standards
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya University Hospital and Nagoya City University Hospital, two of Japan's largest teaching hospitals, operate under the Medical Care Act (医療法). Aichi Prefecture's Medical Care Plan (医療計画) coordinates hospital capacity, emergency medical triage, and specialist care distribution. Hospitals must publish annual quality reports including mortality rates and infection control data under public transparency obligations.
laws.penalty: Hospital accreditation suspension for non-compliance with quality reporting; fines for misrepresenting medical outcomes data
exceptions: Small clinics under 20 beds are exempt from the annual specialist quality report requirement

quiz.q: What must Aichi's major teaching hospitals publish annually under public transparency obligations?
options: Quality reports including mortality rates and infection control data
quiz.explanation: Aichi's major teaching hospitals must publish annual quality reports including mortality rates and infection control data.

laws.title: Nagoya Cochin Chicken Breed Protection
laws.subtitle: Japan's most prized chicken breed has certification standards
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya Cochin (名古屋コーチン) is one of Japan's three prized chicken breeds (日本三大地鶏) and a certified regional brand under Aichi Prefecture's agricultural promotion framework. Only birds raised by certified Aichi producers using the specified lineage and rearing method (free-range, minimum 150 days) may be sold as Nagoya Cochin. The breed is protected under the Plant Variety Protection and Seed Act animal breed registration.
laws.penalty: Civil trademark infringement; fines under the JAS Act for falsely labelling non-certified chicken as Nagoya Cochin
exceptions: Home hobbyist rearing of the breed for personal consumption does not require certification

quiz.q: What is the minimum rearing duration for a chicken to qualify as certified Nagoya Cochin?
quiz.explanation: Certified Nagoya Cochin chickens must be free-range reared for a minimum of 150 days.

laws.title: Aichi Large-Scale Retail Store Opening Procedures
laws.subtitle: New large stores must consult with local communities before opening
laws.fullDescription: Under the Large-Scale Retail Store Location Act (大規模小売店舗立地法), stores over 1,000 sqm in Aichi must submit a location plan to the prefecture and hold public consultations with local community associations before opening. The plan must address traffic congestion, parking, delivery routes, and noise. Aichi municipalities may attach conditions to approval, such as required traffic lights or pedestrian crossings.
laws.penalty: Opening prohibition until consultation and approval process is complete; fines for non-submitted location plans
exceptions: Stores in designated city centre commercial zones with established pedestrian infrastructure have streamlined consultation requirements

quiz.q: What minimum floor area triggers the Large-Scale Retail Store Location Act consultation requirement in Aichi?
quiz.explanation: Stores over 1,000 sqm in Aichi must complete community consultation under the Large-Scale Retail Store Location Act before opening.

laws.title: Aichi Traffic Safety Campaign — Highest Road Mortality History
laws.subtitle: Aichi's past as Japan's most dangerous prefecture shaped strict traffic rules
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture held the grim record of Japan's highest traffic fatalities for 14 consecutive years (1993–2006). This drove Aichi to pioneer strict local traffic safety campaigns under the Road Traffic Act, including mandatory school zone 30km/h zones, enhanced police speed enforcement on national routes, and compulsory reflective gear for cyclists after dark.
laws.penalty: ¥6,000–¥15,000 fines for speeding in 30km/h school zones; ¥5,000 fine for cyclists without reflectors after dark
exceptions: Emergency vehicles are exempt from 30km/h school zone limits during active emergency responses

quiz.q: For how many consecutive years did Aichi hold Japan's record for highest traffic fatalities?
quiz.explanation: Aichi held the record for Japan's highest traffic fatalities for 14 consecutive years (1993–2006), driving strict local road safety rules.

laws.title: Aichi Seismic Retrofit Grant Programme
laws.subtitle: Homeowners can access subsidies to earthquake-proof older homes
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture's Seismic Retrofit Support Programme (耐震改修促進計画) provides free seismic diagnosis and subsidies covering up to two-thirds of retrofit costs for wooden homes built before 1981 in Aichi. Given Aichi's position in the Tokai earthquake zone, the prefecture treats seismic retrofitting as a public safety priority. Nagoya City offers additional top-up grants, making retrofitting effectively free for low-income homeowners.
laws.penalty: No direct penalty for not retrofitting, but non-compliant buildings may face demolition orders if classified as dangerous
exceptions: New homes built after the 1981 Building Standards Act revision are exempt from the subsidy programme

quiz.q: What fraction of seismic retrofit costs does Aichi Prefecture's subsidy cover?
quiz.explanation: Aichi Prefecture's seismic retrofit subsidy covers up to two-thirds of costs for pre-1981 wooden homes.

laws.title: Aichi University City Initiative — Nanzan and Chukyo
laws.subtitle: Major private universities in Aichi must comply with education quality rules
laws.fullDescription: Aichi is home to major private universities including Nanzan University, Chukyo University, and Aichi University. Under the Private School Act (私立学校法) and the Standards for Establishment of Universities (大学設置基準), these institutions must maintain student-faculty ratios, conduct annual self-assessment reports, and submit to MEXT periodic certified quality reviews (認証評価). Universities operating programs with international students must also comply with JASSO scholarship and visa guarantee conditions.
laws.penalty: MEXT suspension of new student enrolment for non-compliant institutions; fines for schools failing accreditation obligations
exceptions: Junior colleges (短期大学) have separate, simplified accreditation pathways

quiz.q: What periodic review must Aichi private universities submit to under MEXT rules?
quiz.explanation: Private universities in Aichi must submit to MEXT-certified quality reviews (認証評価) on a periodic basis.

laws.title: Aichi Health Promotion Prefecture-Wide Campaign
laws.subtitle: Prefecture runs Japan's most comprehensive regional health promotion plan
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture's Aichi Health Plan (健康あいち21) runs in alignment with the national Health Japan 21 campaign under the Health Promotion Act (健康増進法). The plan sets measurable targets for reducing obesity, smoking rates, and diabetes. Employers with over 300 employees in Aichi must submit annual employee health management reports (健康経営) to the prefecture's health insurance coordination bureau.
laws.penalty: Administrative guidance for employers failing to submit health management reports; loss of health management certification for flagrant non-compliance
exceptions: Small businesses under 50 employees are exempt from mandatory annual reporting

quiz.q: What minimum number of employees triggers Aichi's mandatory annual health management reporting requirement for employers?
quiz.explanation: Employers with over 300 employees in Aichi must submit annual employee health management reports.

laws.title: Aichi Renewable Energy Promotion Ordinance
laws.subtitle: New public buildings must install solar panels under prefecture ordinance
laws.fullDescription: Under Aichi Prefecture's Climate Change Action Plan and its Renewable Energy Promotion Ordinance (再生可能エネルギー普及促進条例), all new prefecture-owned public buildings over 500 sqm must install photovoltaic (PV) solar panels covering at least 30% of roof area. Private developers seeking city planning permits for buildings over 2,000 sqm in Nagoya must submit a renewable energy contribution assessment.
laws.penalty: Permits conditioned on inclusion of renewable energy measures; non-compliant public buildings subject to budget review
exceptions: Historically designated buildings and structures in high-shading locations may apply for exemption with supporting assessments

quiz.q: What minimum roof coverage must new Aichi public buildings over 500 sqm have in solar panels?
quiz.explanation: New prefecture-owned public buildings over 500 sqm in Aichi must install PV solar panels covering at least 30% of roof area.

laws.title: Aichi Technical Intern Training Programme Oversight
laws.subtitle: Aichi monitors technical intern trainees more closely than national average
laws.fullDescription: Aichi hosts Japan's second-largest population of Technical Intern Trainees (技能実習生), mostly from Vietnam, China, and Indonesia working in automotive suppliers and food processing. The Aichi Labour Bureau conducts enhanced monitoring under the Technical Intern Training Act (技能実習法) and OTIT oversight. Employers found violating trainee rights (minimum wage, working hours, housing) face programme suspension and public naming.
laws.penalty: Programme suspension for 5 years; public naming of violating employers; criminal prosecution for serious exploitation
exceptions: Employers who self-report minor violations before inspection and provide remediation may receive reduced sanctions

quiz.q: What are the top three source countries for Aichi's Technical Intern Trainees?
quiz.explanation: Aichi's Technical Intern Trainees primarily come from Vietnam, China, and Indonesia, working in automotive suppliers and food processing.

laws.title: Aichi Vacant House Utilisation Programme
laws.subtitle: Prefecture incentivises renovation of vacant homes (akiya) for new residents
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture's Akiya (空き家) Utilisation Programme offers subsidies of up to ¥500,000 for renovation of vacant properties in depopulating areas such as rural Nishi-Mikawa and Higashi-Mikawa. Purchasers who live in the renovated home for at least 5 years qualify for the subsidy. Under the Act on Special Measures for Promotion of Vacant House Measures, municipalities may list dangerous abandoned homes and impose improvement orders on absentee owners.
laws.penalty: Forced demolition at owner cost for homes classified as dangerous; loss of subsidy for purchasers who leave within 5 years
exceptions: Homes used as short-term holiday lets under approved Aichi tourism licences may qualify for subsidy if owner-occupied for more than 180 days per year

quiz.q: What maximum subsidy does Aichi's Akiya programme offer for renovating vacant homes?
quiz.explanation: Aichi's Akiya Utilisation Programme offers subsidies of up to ¥500,000 for renovating vacant properties in depopulating areas.

laws.title: Aichi Cybercrime Division — Automotive IP Theft
laws.subtitle: Aichi Police actively prosecute industrial espionage against auto manufacturers
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefectural Police's Cybercrime Division (サイバー犯罪対策室) focuses heavily on protecting the automotive manufacturing sector from trade secret theft and industrial espionage. Under the Unfair Competition Prevention Act (不正競争防止法), stealing or leaking trade secrets (営業秘密) — including vehicle design files, battery technology, or manufacturing processes — carries enhanced penalties. Aichi police cooperate with Toyota and Denso's internal security teams.
laws.penalty: Up to 10 years imprisonment and ¥3,000,000 fine for theft or disclosure of trade secrets; up to 20 years for overseas disclosure
exceptions: Whistle-blowing on illegal conduct through proper legal channels is protected under the Public Interest Disclosure Act

quiz.q: What is the maximum sentence for disclosing automotive trade secrets overseas from Aichi under Japanese law?
quiz.explanation: Overseas disclosure of trade secrets under Japan's Unfair Competition Prevention Act carries up to 20 years imprisonment.

laws.title: Nagoya Port Festival and Fireworks Rules
laws.subtitle: Major harbour events require prefecture-level safety coordination
laws.fullDescription: The Nagoya Port Festival (名古屋みなと祭) and its fireworks display (one of Japan's largest) attract over 1 million visitors annually. Under Aichi Prefecture's Large Event Safety Ordinance and the Explosives Control Act (火薬類取締法), fireworks displays require Aichi Prefectural Police and Fire Department co-approval. Crowd management plans must be submitted 30 days in advance for events over 50,000 expected attendees.
laws.penalty: Event cancellation and fines up to ¥1,000,000 for operating fireworks without approval; criminal liability for explosives violations
exceptions: Traditional small-scale neighbourhood (町内会) fireworks under 1kg of powder are exempt from the full approval process

quiz.q: How many visitors does the annual Nagoya Port Festival fireworks display attract?
quiz.explanation: The Nagoya Port Festival fireworks display attracts over 1 million visitors annually, making it one of Japan's largest.

laws.title: Aichi Expo 2005 Legacy Fund Rules
laws.subtitle: Post-Expo land in Nagakute operates under special development rules
laws.fullDescription: The site of Expo 2005 Aichi, now Moricoro Park (愛・地球博記念公園) in Nagakute City, operates under the Expo Legacy Fund administered by Aichi Prefecture. Redevelopment of park facilities must follow the Expo 2005 Legacy Plan, preserving green space ratios and public access. The Ghibli Park (ジブリパーク), opened 2022 within the site, required an Aichi Prefecture Special Cultural Development Permit under the legacy framework.
laws.penalty: Permit withdrawal for developments that reduce public green space below the Expo Legacy Plan minimum ratios
exceptions: Cultural and educational facility construction that increases public programming may receive expedited permits

quiz.q: What popular entertainment facility opened within the Expo 2005 site in Nagakute in 2022?
quiz.explanation: Ghibli Park opened in 2022 within the former Expo 2005 site at Moricoro Park in Nagakute, Aichi.

laws.title: Osu Kannon Shopping District Vendor Rules
laws.subtitle: Nagoya's most eclectic shopping street has commercial ordinances
laws.fullDescription: Osu Shopping Arcade (大須商店街) in Nagoya, one of Japan's liveliest covered shopping streets, is governed by Nagoya City's commercial zone ordinances and the Osu Shopping District Association's self-regulatory code. Street food vendors must hold city food hygiene licences and are restricted to designated pitches. Cosplay events in the arcade require advance notification to the ward office and police for crowd management.
laws.penalty: Fines ¥20,000–¥100,000 for unlicensed food vending in the arcade; civil penalties for damage to arcade structure
exceptions: Registered arcade tenants may operate within their own frontage without additional street trading licences

quiz.q: What event type in Osu Shopping Arcade requires advance notification to the ward office and police?
quiz.explanation: Cosplay events in Osu Shopping Arcade require advance notification to the ward office and police for crowd management.

laws.title: Aichi Forest Management and Timber Certification
laws.subtitle: Aichi's forestry industry must comply with sustainable timber rules
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture, with extensive forested areas in the Higashi-Mikawa region, enforces the Forestry Act (森林法) and its own Forest Management Plan (森林整備計画). Commercial timber harvesting requires a harvest permission (伐採届) filed with the municipal forest board. Timber sold commercially must carry FSC or SGEC sustainability certification under national green procurement guidelines for public procurement.
laws.penalty: Fines up to ¥1,000,000 for harvesting without notification; disqualification from public procurement contracts for non-certified timber suppliers
exceptions: Personal firewood harvesting under 5 cubic metres per year from own land requires only simplified notification

quiz.q: What sustainability certifications does Aichi require for timber used in public procurement?
quiz.explanation: Aichi requires FSC or SGEC sustainability certification for timber used in public procurement contracts.

laws.title: Aichi Women in Manufacturing Support Rules
laws.subtitle: Prefecture promotes gender equality in male-dominated automotive sector
laws.fullDescription: Under the Act on Promotion of Women's Active Engagement in Professional Life (女性活躍推進法), companies in Aichi with over 101 employees must publish gender pay gap data and set targets for women in management roles. Aichi Prefecture's Women's Active Participation Plan (あいち女性の活躍促進プラン) targets 30% women in management at major Aichi manufacturers by 2030. Toyota and Denso are among the signatories.
laws.penalty: Public disclosure of non-compliant companies; loss of Aichi Prefecture supplier certification for persistent non-compliance
exceptions: Companies under 101 employees have a voluntary reporting framework

quiz.q: What is Aichi Prefecture's target percentage of women in management at major manufacturers by 2030?
quiz.explanation: Aichi's Women's Active Participation Plan targets 30% women in management at major manufacturers by 2030.

laws.title: Meitetsu Railway Regional Fare Integration Rules
laws.subtitle: Private railways and city buses must coordinate fares for IC card users
laws.fullDescription: Meitetsu (名古屋鉄道), Aichi's major private railway network, and Nagoya's city bus and subway system participate in the Manaca (マナカ) IC card fare integration system under MLIT guidelines. Through-fare calculations for multi-modal journeys must be transparent and IC card discounts may not be offered selectively in a way that disadvantages non-IC card users above a 10% differential.
laws.penalty: MLIT improvement orders for fare system violations; civil claims for systematic overcharging
exceptions: Special discount schemes targeting elderly and disabled passengers may be offered on IC cards without triggering the 10% differential rule
laws.sourceLabel: Meitetsu Railway / Manaca IC Card System

quiz.q: What is the name of the IC card system used on Meitetsu and Nagoya city transport?
quiz.explanation: Manaca (マナカ) is the IC card system used on Meitetsu Railway and Nagoya city buses and subway.

laws.title: Aichi Barrier-Free Transport Act Implementation
laws.subtitle: Aichi enforces accessibility standards at all major transport hubs
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture's Barrier-Free Basic Plan (バリアフリー基本計画) implements the Barrier-Free Act with enhanced local targets. All stations with over 3,000 daily users must be fully step-free by 2025. Nagoya's underground walkway network connecting the subway to major buildings must maintain tactile paving, auditory guidance, and step-free routes throughout. The Aichi Barrier-Free Awards recognise exemplary implementation.
laws.penalty: City may withhold building permits for non-compliant new transport-adjacent construction; existing stations receive improvement orders
exceptions: Rural stations on low-use lines may apply for extended compliance timelines with ridership justification

quiz.q: What daily user threshold triggers Aichi's mandatory full step-free access requirement at stations?
quiz.explanation: Aichi stations with over 3,000 daily users must be fully step-free by 2025 under the prefecture's Barrier-Free Basic Plan.

laws.title: Aichi Arts Center Public Art Maintenance Rules
laws.subtitle: Permanent public artworks in Nagoya must be maintained by commissioning bodies
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Arts Center (愛知芸術文化センター) and Nagoya City Art Museum jointly administer the Aichi Triennale contemporary art festival, one of Japan's largest. Public artworks commissioned under the Aichi Triennale's civic art programme must be maintained by the commissioning body (typically Nagoya City) for a minimum of 10 years under Nagoya's Public Art Management Guidelines. Controversial works may be removed only after a formal review by the Aichi Art Advisory Council.
laws.penalty: City may seek civil damages from artists or organizers for unauthorised removal of commissioned public artworks within the 10-year minimum period
exceptions: Works that pose public safety risks may be removed immediately with a formal safety report

quiz.q: What is the minimum maintenance period for public artworks commissioned under Nagoya's civic art programme?
quiz.explanation: Public artworks commissioned under Nagoya's civic art programme must be maintained for a minimum of 10 years.

laws.title: Aichi Hometown Tax Regional Specialities
laws.subtitle: Aichi municipalities offer automotive and food gifts through furusato nozei
laws.fullDescription: Aichi municipalities participating in the Hometown Tax (ふるさと納税) system offer distinctive regional return gifts (返礼品) including Nagoya Cochin products, Aichi ceramics (瀬戸焼, Seto-yaki), Toyota merchandise, and premium Nagoya-meshi food sets. Under the Local Tax Act, gifts must not exceed 30% of donation value and must be locally produced or manufactured in Aichi. The most popular Aichi donation destination is Nagoya City.
laws.penalty: Loss of central government equalisation grants for municipalities offering non-compliant gifts
exceptions: Experience-based gifts (local cooking classes, factory tours) are valued by market rate rather than production cost

quiz.q: What traditional Aichi ceramic style is commonly offered as a Hometown Tax return gift?
quiz.explanation: Seto-yaki (瀬戸焼) ceramics from Seto City, Aichi are a popular return gift through the Hometown Tax system.

laws.title: Aichi Heat Stroke Prevention Ordinance
laws.subtitle: Japan's hottest major city has mandatory heat countermeasures
laws.fullDescription: Nagoya consistently records Japan's highest summer temperatures among major cities. Aichi Prefecture's Heat Stroke Prevention Ordinance (熱中症対策推進条例), enacted 2021, requires all outdoor event organisers in summer (June–September) to provide free drinking water stations and shaded rest areas. Construction site operators must implement mandatory cooling breaks during heat alerts. Employers who force outdoor work without countermeasures during extreme heat advisories face administrative sanctions.
laws.penalty: Event cancellation orders for non-compliant summer events; administrative sanctions and fines for employers ignoring heat advisory protocols
exceptions: Indoor air-conditioned facilities are exempt from outdoor heat countermeasure requirements

quiz.q: When did Aichi Prefecture enact its Heat Stroke Prevention Ordinance?
quiz.explanation: Aichi's Heat Stroke Prevention Ordinance was enacted in 2021 in response to Nagoya's record summer temperatures.

laws.title: Aichi Tea Culture and Seto Ceramics Tea Ceremony Rules
laws.subtitle: Prefecture protects the intersection of ceramics and tea ceremony heritage
laws.fullDescription: Aichi's Seto City and Tokoname City are home to two of Japan's six ancient kiln sites (六古窯). Tea ceremony vessels produced in Seto and Tokoname are designated Traditional Craft Products under the Act for the Promotion of Traditional Craft Industries. Potters using the certified traditional techniques must hold apprentice records and register with the Aichi Traditional Craft Industry Cooperative. The craft certification may not be used on machine-produced pieces.
laws.penalty: Removal of Traditional Craft certification; fines for misleading use of traditional craft designation on mass-produced goods
exceptions: Contemporary designers using traditional kilns may produce non-certified modern pieces without the designation
laws.sourceLabel: METI Traditional Craft Designation — Seto & Tokoname

quiz.q: How many of Japan's six ancient kiln sites (六古窯) are located in Aichi Prefecture?
quiz.explanation: Two of Japan's six ancient kiln sites are in Aichi: Seto City and Tokoname City.

laws.title: Aichi Online Secondhand Goods Market Regulation
laws.subtitle: Online resellers in Aichi must hold an antiquarian dealer licence
laws.fullDescription: Under the Act on Dealing in Secondhand Goods (古物営業法) as enforced by Aichi Prefectural Police, any person who regularly buys and resells goods — including through online platforms like Mercari or Yahoo Auctions — is legally required to hold a secondhand goods dealer licence (古物商許可) issued by Aichi police. Applications cost ¥19,000. Professional resellers without a licence commit a criminal offence even if operating entirely online.
laws.penalty: Up to 3 years imprisonment or ¥1,000,000 fine for operating as an unlicensed secondhand goods dealer
exceptions: Occasional personal sales (less than a defined frequency and value) do not constitute 'dealing' under the Act

quiz.q: How much does it cost to apply for a secondhand goods dealer licence (古物商許可) in Aichi?
quiz.explanation: The secondhand goods dealer licence application in Aichi costs ¥19,000, issued by Aichi Prefectural Police.

laws.title: Aichi Nankai Trough Mega-Earthquake Preparedness
laws.subtitle: Prefecture prepares for a magnitude 9 Nankai Trough event
laws.fullDescription: The Cabinet Office estimates a Nankai Trough mega-earthquake (南海トラフ巨大地震) could strike within the next 30 years with 70–80% probability, potentially causing tsunami run-up of up to 6 metres in parts of Aichi. Under the Nankai Trough Earthquake Special Measures Act (南海トラフ地震対策特別措置法), Aichi municipalities in coastal hazard areas must complete evacuation route upgrades by 2030. Businesses designated as critical infrastructure must prepare and test Business Continuity Plans (BCP) annually.
laws.penalty: Administrative guidance for critical infrastructure businesses that have not prepared BCPs; fines for local governments that fail tsunami sign requirements
exceptions: Inland municipalities in low seismic risk zones have reduced preparedness obligations

quiz.q: What is the estimated probability of a Nankai Trough mega-earthquake within 30 years, affecting Aichi?
quiz.explanation: The Cabinet Office estimates a 70–80% probability of a Nankai Trough mega-earthquake within 30 years, posing a major tsunami threat to Aichi's coast.

laws.title: Aichi Prefectural Animal Welfare Ordinance
laws.subtitle: Dogs and cats must be registered, vaccinated, and not abandoned
laws.fullDescription: Under Aichi's Animal Welfare Ordinance (動物の愛護及び管理に関する条例) and the national Act on Welfare and Management of Animals (動物愛護管理法), all dogs must be registered with the municipal government and vaccinated against rabies annually. Cats must be microchipped if sold or given away as of 2022. Animal abandonment is a criminal offence. Aichi operates a prefecture shelter and promotes zero-euthanasia through an active adoption programme.
laws.penalty: Up to ¥1,000,000 fine or 1 year imprisonment for animal abandonment; ¥20,000 for failing to register a dog
exceptions: Working farm animals used in agricultural production are subject to different welfare standards under agricultural regulations

quiz.q: Since which year are cats in Aichi required to be microchipped when sold or given away?
quiz.explanation: Since 2022, cats must be microchipped when sold or given away in Aichi under the amended national animal welfare law.

laws.title: Aichi Anti-Stalking Enforcement Rules
laws.subtitle: Aichi Police provide 24-hour stalking consultation and rapid response
laws.fullDescription: Under the Stalker Control Law (ストーカー規制法) as enhanced in 2021, Aichi Prefectural Police operate a 24-hour anti-stalking consultation line and must respond to complaints within 24 hours. Police may issue a warning (警告) to a suspected stalker on first complaint without the victim's formal complaint in emergency circumstances. GPS tracking of another person without consent is explicitly prohibited under the 2021 amendment.
laws.penalty: Up to 1 year imprisonment or ¥1,000,000 fine for violating a restraining order; up to 2 years for GPS stalking without consent
exceptions: Parental GPS monitoring of minor children with their knowledge is not covered by the stalking law

quiz.q: What was explicitly prohibited under Japan's 2021 Stalker Control Law amendment?
options: GPS tracking of another person without consent
quiz.explanation: GPS tracking of another person without their consent was explicitly prohibited under Japan's 2021 amendment to the Stalker Control Law.

laws.title: Aichi Global 300 Foreign Talent Attraction Programme
laws.subtitle: Prefecture recruits skilled foreign professionals to manufacturing and tech sectors
laws.fullDescription: Aichi's Global 300 Programme offers preferential processing and support to foreign nationals with specialist skills in automotive engineering, AI, and advanced manufacturing who relocate to Aichi. Participating companies must provide housing assistance and Japanese language training. Foreign highly skilled professionals (高度専門職) under Japan's points-based visa system may receive accelerated permanent residency review in as little as 1 year when residing in Aichi.
laws.penalty: No penalty; voluntary programme — misrepresentation of qualifications may affect visa status under immigration law
exceptions: Professionals who leave Aichi within 3 years of receiving programme benefits may be required to repay housing support grants

quiz.q: How quickly may highly skilled foreign professionals in Aichi receive accelerated permanent residency review?
quiz.explanation: Foreign highly skilled professionals under Japan's points-based visa system in Aichi may receive accelerated permanent residency review in as little as 1 year.

laws.title: Aichi 8020 Dental Health Campaign
laws.subtitle: Prefecture targets 80% of elderly residents keeping 20 teeth at age 80
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture's 8020 Campaign (80才で20本の歯を) targets 80% of residents aged 80 retaining at least 20 natural teeth, aligning with national goals. Aichi subsidises dental check-ups for adults at ages 20, 40, 50, 60, and 70 under the prefecture's Health Promotion Plan. Employers with over 50 employees are encouraged (but not required) to subsidise annual dental check-ups for all employees.
laws.penalty: No penalties — voluntary public health campaign; non-participating dentists are not penalised
exceptions: Routine dental procedures covered by national health insurance are administered under separate national rules

quiz.q: What does Aichi's '8020 Campaign' target?
quiz.explanation: Aichi's 8020 Campaign targets 80% of residents aged 80 retaining at least 20 natural teeth.

laws.title: Mikawa Bay Clam Aquaculture Regulations
laws.subtitle: Asari clam harvesting in Mikawa Bay is regulated by Aichi Fisheries Cooperative
laws.fullDescription: Asari clams (あさり) from Mikawa Bay are Aichi's most valuable marine product. The Aichi Fisheries Cooperative issues annual harvest quotas and size limits (minimum 2cm shell length) under the Fisheries Act (漁業法). Non-cooperative members harvesting clams commercially require a prefectural fishing licence. Harmful algal bloom (赤潮) alerts trigger temporary harvesting bans across affected zones.
laws.penalty: Up to ¥1,000,000 fine for unlicensed commercial harvesting; licence suspension for quota violations
exceptions: Personal non-commercial gathering of up to 2kg per day per person is permitted during open season

quiz.q: What is the minimum shell length for legally harvestable asari clams in Mikawa Bay?
quiz.explanation: Asari clams must have a minimum shell length of 2cm to be legally harvested in Mikawa Bay, Aichi.

laws.title: Aichi Creative Economy Freelance Support
laws.subtitle: Aichi provides dispute resolution services for freelancers in creative industries
laws.fullDescription: Under the Freelance Protection Act (特定受託事業者に係る取引の適正化等に関する法律, 2024) and Aichi Prefecture's Business Environment Improvement Plan, freelancers and sole traders providing services to businesses in Aichi are entitled to written contracts for any engagement over 60 days. Aichi Prefecture's Business Dispute Resolution Centre offers free mediation for freelance payment disputes. Businesses that routinely fail to provide contracts may be publicly named.
laws.penalty: Fines under the Freelance Protection Act for repeated failure to issue written contracts; public naming by Aichi Prefecture
exceptions: One-off transactions under ¥50,000 between individuals are exempt from written contract requirements
laws.sourceLabel: Aichi Prefecture Business Dispute Resolution Centre

quiz.q: What engagement duration triggers the written contract requirement for freelancers in Aichi under the 2024 Freelance Protection Act?
quiz.explanation: Freelancers in Aichi are entitled to written contracts for any engagement over 60 days under Japan's 2024 Freelance Protection Act.

laws.title: Aichi Green Building Certification Requirements
laws.subtitle: New large buildings must meet CASBEE environmental performance standards
laws.fullDescription: Under Nagoya City's Environmental Action Plan and the Energy Conservation Act (省エネ法), all new buildings over 5,000 sqm in Nagoya must obtain CASBEE (Comprehensive Assessment System for Built Environment Efficiency) certification, Japan's building environmental performance standard. Buildings receiving CASBEE S-rank (Excellent) certification receive a fast-tracked planning permit process and city promotional listing.
laws.penalty: Building permits conditioned on CASBEE assessment submission; non-compliance with energy conservation standards triggers improvement orders
exceptions: Heritage building renovations are assessed against modified baseline standards that account for historic structure limitations

quiz.q: What building environmental performance certification does Nagoya require for new buildings over 5,000 sqm?
quiz.explanation: Nagoya requires CASBEE certification — Japan's building environmental performance standard — for new buildings over 5,000 sqm.

laws.title: Aichi Repeat Offender Monitoring Programme
laws.subtitle: Released serious offenders are subject to prefectural monitoring under parole rules
laws.fullDescription: Under the Act for Probationary Supervision of Persons Who Committed Specified Offences (再犯防止推進法), Aichi Prefecture's Regional Re-offending Prevention Council coordinates between Aichi Probation Office, local governments, and employers. Persons released from prison who committed sex offences against minors are subject to GPS-tracked monitoring in Aichi. All parolees must register their residence within 24 hours of release.
laws.penalty: Return to custody for parolees who fail to register residence or comply with monitoring conditions
exceptions: First-time minor offenders on summary probation are not subject to GPS monitoring

quiz.q: Within how many hours must parolees in Aichi register their residence after release?
quiz.explanation: All parolees in Aichi must register their residence with the Probation Office within 24 hours of release from custody.

laws.title: Toyota Proving Ground Road Closure Notices
laws.subtitle: Vehicle test roads in Toyota City require public notification when used
laws.fullDescription: Toyota Motor Corporation's proving grounds and test tracks in Toyota City operate under Road Traffic Act special permits. When test vehicles use public roads in Toyota City for endurance trials, Aichi Prefectural Police and Toyota City must issue advance public notices. Prototype vehicles may be disguised but must carry all required reflectors, registration plates, and lights. Accident liability during authorised test drives is governed by Toyota's public road test permit conditions.
laws.penalty: Revocation of public road test permit for accidents caused by non-compliant test vehicles
exceptions: Fully enclosed private proving grounds are exempt from public notification requirements

quiz.q: What must prototype vehicles doing road tests on public roads in Toyota City carry?
options: All required reflectors, registration plates, and lights
A safety observer vehicle behind them
A special red flag at the front
quiz.explanation: Prototype vehicles on public road tests in Toyota City must carry all required reflectors, registration plates, and lights despite any external disguise.

laws.title: Aichi EV Transition Support Scheme
laws.subtitle: Prefecture subsidises electric vehicle adoption for businesses and residents
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture's EV Promotion Programme provides subsidies of up to ¥200,000 for individuals and ¥500,000 for businesses purchasing zero-emission vehicles for use in Aichi. As Japan's automotive manufacturing centre, Aichi has a strategic interest in transitioning to EVs domestically. Eligible vehicles must be from models certified under the Low Emission Vehicle (低公害車) designation. Subsidy recipients must register the vehicle in Aichi and keep it for at least 3 years.
laws.penalty: Subsidy clawback if the vehicle is deregistered from Aichi or sold within 3 years of purchase
exceptions: Commercial fleet operators replacing multiple vehicles may apply for the business subsidy per vehicle up to a fleet cap of 10 vehicles

quiz.q: What is the maximum EV subsidy available to businesses in Aichi?
quiz.explanation: Aichi's EV Promotion Programme offers businesses subsidies of up to ¥500,000 per qualifying zero-emission vehicle.

laws.title: Aichi Traditional Performing Arts — Puppet Theatre
laws.subtitle: Bunraku and ningyo joruri troupes in Aichi have heritage protection
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture has a rich tradition of Bunraku-style ningyo joruri (人形浄瑠璃) puppet theatre, particularly in the Ama and Tsushima areas. Performing troupes designated as Prefectural Intangible Cultural Property (県指定無形文化財) receive annual operational subsidies and must perform publicly at least twice per year. Costumes, puppets, and stage instruments are registered as associated cultural properties and may not be sold overseas without prefecture approval.
laws.penalty: Loss of designation and subsidy for troupes that fail to meet public performance requirements; fines for unauthorised overseas sale of registered cultural property items
exceptions: Short-term international tours with cultural exchange approval from the prefecture are permitted

quiz.q: What is the minimum number of public performances required annually for Aichi's designated ningyo joruri troupes?
quiz.explanation: Aichi's designated ningyo joruri puppet theatre troupes must perform publicly at least twice per year to retain their heritage designation.

laws.title: Aichi Consumer Contract Review — Automotive Sales Practices
laws.subtitle: High-pressure auto dealership sales tactics are specifically regulated
laws.fullDescription: Aichi's Prefectural Consumer Affairs Centre receives the highest number of automotive sales complaints in Japan due to the density of dealerships. Under the Consumer Contract Act (消費者契約法) and Specified Commercial Transactions Act, dealers who use high-pressure tactics, prevent customers from leaving the dealership, or misrepresent finance terms void the resulting contract. Customers have a statutory 8-day cooling-off period for door-to-door auto sales.
laws.penalty: Contract rescission; fines up to ¥3,000,000 for systematic misleading sales practices; dealer licence revocation for repeat offences
exceptions: Sales through standard showroom visits where the customer came voluntarily are not covered by cooling-off (unless high pressure is demonstrated)

quiz.q: Why does Aichi receive Japan's highest number of automotive sales complaints?
options: Cars are more expensive in Aichi
Aichi has the highest density of car dealerships due to the automotive industry
Aichi has weaker consumer protection laws
Dealerships target foreign workers in Aichi
quiz.explanation: Aichi's density of automotive dealerships — due to the Toyota-centred industry — generates Japan's highest volume of automotive sales complaints.

laws.title: Aichi Personal Information Protection Ordinance
laws.subtitle: Prefecture enforces strict rules on public and private handling of personal data
laws.fullDescription: Aichi Prefecture's Personal Information Protection Ordinance (個人情報保護条例), aligned with the national Act on the Protection of Personal Information (個人情報の保護に関する法律, APPI), requires all prefecture-level organisations and businesses with over 5,000 records of personal data to appoint a data protection officer, maintain an incident response plan, and report data breaches to the prefecture within 72 hours.
laws.penalty: Fines up to ¥1,000,000 for failure to report data breaches; criminal penalties under national APPI for wilful misuse of personal data
exceptions: Academic research and statistical purposes have conditional exemptions for data processing with appropriate anonymisation
laws.sourceLabel: Aichi Prefecture Personal Information Protection Office

quiz.q: Within how many hours must Aichi businesses report data breaches to the prefecture?
quiz.explanation: Businesses in Aichi must report data breaches to the prefecture within 72 hours under the Personal Information Protection Ordinance.

laws.title: Aichi Critical Infrastructure Business Continuity Rules
laws.subtitle: Toyota and other designated essential businesses must have tested BCPs
laws.fullDescription: Under Japan's Re-offending Prevention and Business Continuity Act framework and Aichi Prefecture's Critical Infrastructure Protection Plan, businesses designated as critical infrastructure (自動車産業中核企業) — including Toyota, Denso, Aisin, and their Tier 1 suppliers — must submit Business Continuity Plans (BCP) to Aichi Prefecture, conduct annual tabletop exercises, and achieve a minimum of 72-hour operational continuity after a major earthquake. Supply chain resilience is a key national security concern given Aichi's role in Japan's economy.
laws.penalty: Administrative guidance; loss of prefecture emergency response partnership status for non-compliant designated businesses
exceptions: Tier 2 and below suppliers with under 300 employees have a voluntary BCP framework rather than mandatory submission
laws.sourceLabel: Aichi Prefecture Critical Infrastructure Protection Plan

quiz.q: What minimum operational continuity period must Aichi's critical infrastructure businesses achieve after a major earthquake?
quiz.explanation: Aichi's designated critical infrastructure businesses must achieve a minimum of 72-hour operational continuity after a major earthquake.
